finding: §1 still ships the release that §3 says was cut, and it is the first thing an implementer reads. Lines 20-24: 'Two deliverables, and only the first is a no-op by default. §2 ships audit_converge_on ... §3 changes consecutive_clean and converged for any project whose spec moves between rounds, opted in or not. An earlier draft of this paragraph claimed the whole release was behaviour-preserving; it is not, and §3 is why.' §3 is now titled 'What this release deliberately does not contain' and its whole content is the removal of that mechanism. So §1 names a second deliverable that does not exist, describes a behaviour change to consecutive_clean and converged that nothing in §2, §4 or §5 implements, and asserts the release is not behaviour-preserving when after the cut it is (§2's default is all, 'the behaviour tp ships today, so no existing project changes'). §1 was not edited this round, so the defect is newly created by the removal rather than carried: an implementer building from §1 builds a spec-hash reset that §3 spent a section explaining why not to build, and one reading §1 and §3 in order cannot tell which is current. §5 has no test for a reset, which is the only place the contradiction resolves.
suggestion: Rewrite §1's second paragraph for the single-deliverable release: one deliverable (§2's field), a no-op by default, and a pointer to §3 for what was cut. Delete the 'it is not, and §3 is why' sentence — after the cut the release IS behaviour-preserving for a project that does not set the field, and that is now §2.1's whole argument for the default.

finding: Two §4 sentences describe the cut mechanism as present, and one of them is load-bearing for a Non-Goal's argument. (1) Non-Goal 4: 'review_converge_on is unchanged. §3 adds a function rather than altering the shared one precisely so review's --status cannot move.' §3 adds no function; nothing in this release adds one, so the reason Non-Goal 4 gives for its own guarantee no longer exists and an implementer cannot tell whether a new function is still required of them. (2) The guard-reversal paragraph: 'assert.Len(t, e, 3, "a streak entry carries role, consecutive_clean and open only") ... and which §3's reset touches.' There is no reset, so the stated reason for singling that assertion out is gone — while the assertion itself is real (audit_signal_test.go:498, verified) and is what §5 test 11 pins.
suggestion: Non-Goal 4: state the guarantee without the cut mechanism — 'review_converge_on is unchanged; this release adds a separate audit-side predicate rather than widening engine.ValidReviewConvergeOn or the review clean walk, so review's --status cannot move.' Guard paragraph: drop 'and which §3's reset touches'; :498 earns its place because it is the mutation-killing assertion in the file, which the sentence already says.

finding: §4's guard-reversal paragraph now points past the end of §5: 'Non-Goal 2 keeps the first two true; §5 test 12 pins all nine.' §5 contains eleven numbered tests (1-11); there is no test 12. The intended target is test 11, 'The nine surviving assertions of TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate still pass, including :498's streak-entry shape.' Round 5 reported this pointer as wrong when it read 'test 9'; the repair moved it to 12, which is a dangling reference rather than a wrong one — strictly worse, because a reader who checks it finds nothing at all and cannot infer which test was meant. The eleven-assertion count the same paragraph makes is correct (verified: audit_signal_test.go:473,474,481,484,485,490,493,494,497,498,500 = 11 assert/require calls in the function), so only the §5 pointer is wrong.
suggestion: Change 'test 12' to 'test 11'. Since this is the second failed repair of the same pointer, bind it to something that cannot rot: name the test by its title ('§5's "The nine surviving assertions"') rather than by its ordinal, as §2.2 should too.

finding: §2.2's closing sentence still points at the wrong §5 item after the repair. It reads '§5 test 5 uses a legacy row because it is convenient and real, not because the case is live.' §5 test 5 is '**warning is advisory**, tested separately from info because warning is 158 of the corpus's 360 non-PASS rows' — it uses no legacy row and says nothing about one. The test that does is test 7, 'Unrecognised fails closed', whose own text reads 'because a legacy row supplies only (a): all 67 carry a present, non-null high/medium/low'. Round 5 reported this sentence pointing at test 4; the repair moved it one item to test 5 rather than to test 7, so the claim §2.2 makes about the test suite is still false and a reader verifying §2.2's argument against §5 finds it unsupported.
suggestion: Point at test 7, or better name it: '§5's "Unrecognised fails closed" uses a legacy row for case (a) because it is convenient and real, not because the case is live.'

finding: §2 assigns this release a sweep whose targets are already swept, so the instruction has no work in it and its remaining effect is to send a unit to edit correct text. §2: 'it still stands in two other places this release must sweep: skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:519-522 states it as *the* rule for workflow fields, and spec/0.31.0.md:41 carries it for the twin. REFERENCE.md:327-328 additionally names TP_RUN_MAX_UNITS and TP_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS.' Measured in the working tree today: REFERENCE.md:521-525 states 'The chain differs by field kind' and then 'workflow fields  task-file workflow override > .tp/config.json > built-in default' — three layers, already correct, with the five-layer form nowhere on the page. spec/0.31.0.md:41 reads 'It resolves like every other workflow field (task override > project config > built-in default — this sentence read CLI > env > task override > project config > built-in default until v0.37.0's review round 5 ...)' — corrected, and it records its own correction. REFERENCE.md:328-330 names the two variables only inside a parenthetical that says they do not exist ('neither variable exists in any non-test source, and workflow fields have no env layer to ignore'). All three named defects are gone; a unit given this sentence as spec cover either closes the task with no diff, or 'fixes' the disclaimers that are the repair.
suggestion: Delete the sweep instruction and the three citations, or restate it as done: 'the five-layer form has been corrected in CLAUDE.md, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md and spec/0.31.0.md; this release adds no further sweep.' Two further points for whoever edits it: a measured file:line claim like this one goes stale between rounds by construction, so bind it to a guard (docs_contract_test.go already asserts REFERENCE.md content) rather than to a line number; and note that spec/0.31.0.md — a shipped historical spec — has now been edited, which v0.34.0 §11 Non-Goal 6 rules out ('Historical specs are records; the living docs were corrected'), so if any sweep target is a past spec the release must say why that rule is being set aside.

finding: §2's fence cost — 'Widening it is two new call sites in two files' — omits the two edits without which those call sites do nothing, and the omission fails silently in the direction of an unfenced field. fenceWorkflowWrite (internal/cli/unattended.go:56-76) returns early unless engine.FencedCapField(field) is true, and that predicate is backed by var fencedCapFields (internal/engine/unattended.go:46-54), a fixed map of seven numeric fields. It then reads engine.ResolvedCapValue(&wf, field) — a switch over those same seven, returning (float64, bool) — and engine.UnattendedRaise(field, requested, resolved), whose whole semantics is an ordinal comparison. So a string branch that calls fenceWorkflowWrite("audit_converge_on", ???) has no float to pass, and if it passes one anyway the call returns at the FencedCapField guard as a no-op: the field ships documented as fenced and is not. The real change is (a) a fenced-set entry or a second predicate, (b) a non-ordinal refusal path, and only then (c) the two call sites. One consequence to decide with it: engine/unattended_test.go:69 asserts FencedCapField("review_clean_rounds") is false, commented 'a convergence count is not a budget' — adding a convergence-policy field to fencedCapFields contradicts that shipped assertion's stated rationale, so the fenced set is probably the wrong home.
suggestion: State the mechanism, not just the cost: e.g. 'a new engine.FencedPolicyField(field) predicate plus refuseUnattendedPolicyField(field), called from the audit_converge_on branch of set.go and set_project.go — the cap fence's ordinal comparison does not apply and fencedCapFields is left alone, since unattended_test.go:69 already says a convergence field is not a budget.' Then §5 test 9's failing arm is real: an implementation that reuses fenceWorkflowWrite unchanged exits 0 under TP_UNATTENDED and the test reddens.

finding: The fence's trigger is specified for exactly one of the field's two values, and the two readings are not equivalent. §2 names 'tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=blocking' and its --project form; §5 test 9 asserts those two commands exit 2 under TP_UNATTENDED=1 and 0 without it. Neither says what 'tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=all' does under the variable. Both answers are defensible and the spec picks neither: refuse every write of the field (simple, and it means a unit cannot restore the strict value either), or refuse only the relaxing value, mirroring the cap fence, which by engine.UnattendedRaise accepts an equal-or-lower value precisely because 'lowering a budget cannot manufacture convergence' (internal/engine/unattended.go:70-73). The string field has no ordering, so 'relaxing' has to be enumerated by hand — blocking is weak, all is strict — and nothing in §2 does that. Test 9 cannot discriminate: it drives only =blocking, so both implementations pass it identically, which is the same shape of hole §5's own preamble says the naming rule exists to prevent.
suggestion: Add one sentence to §2 — 'Under TP_UNATTENDED a write of audit_converge_on is refused when the requested value is blocking; audit_converge_on=all is a tightening and is accepted' (or 'any write of the field is refused', if that is the choice) — and add the matching arm to test 9 so the unchosen reading fails.

finding: §2 promises the twin's validation behaviour and names none of the sinks that deliver it, and the missing half is the one that decides what happens when the gate predicate is handed a value it cannot grade. review_converge_on validates in FOUR places, two per exit code: set.go:375 and set_project.go:68 reject a bad literal argument as a usage error (exit 2), and review_status.go:39 and review_record.go:48 reject an invalid RESOLVED value from a stored layer as a validation error (exit 1), each with engine.ReviewConvergeOnHint. §2 states only 'rejected with the same hint machinery when the value is neither', and §5 test 2 only 'an invalid value is refused with the same hint shape review_converge_on uses' — no exit code, no command. An implementation that validates at the two set commands alone passes test 2 while a hand-edited .tp/config.json carrying audit_converge_on: "bogus" reaches the clean predicate at tp audit --record, where the release's own fail-closed rule is written for a row's severity and not for the knob: the round is then graded under whichever branch the switch falls through to, silently. This is the exact question the round asks about error paths — which exit code, which command, which hint.
suggestion: State it: 'A bad literal at tp set --workflow or its --project form is a usage error (exit 2). An invalid resolved value reaching tp audit <spec> --record or tp audit <spec> --status is a validation error (exit 1) with the same hint, mirroring review_status.go:39 and review_record.go:48; an unrecognised resolved value is never treated as a policy.' Add a §5 test whose input is a stored bogus value winning resolution, asserting exit 1 on both audit sinks — an implementation validating only at the set commands fails it.

finding: §4's counted claim 'One shipped guard is deliberately reversed' is false: a second shipped guard pins a documented sentence this release makes untrue, and neither §4 nor §5 accounts for it. internal/cli/docs_contract_test.go:96 defines divergenceCountingSubstring = "audit convergence still counts every non-PASS row" and TestDocsCarryTheConvergenceSignalWording (:130-133) asserts skills/tp/SKILL.md contains it verbatim. Under audit_converge_on: blocking that sentence is no longer true, so the release is in a fork it never names: update SKILL.md as CLAUDE.md's pre-release checklist requires and this shipped test reddens with no spec cover for touching it; leave SKILL.md alone and tp ships a feature whose own driver-facing documentation states the opposite rule. §4 spends a paragraph counting the eleven assertions of the one guard it did find, which is exactly the uniqueness-over-an-unenumerated-set shape CLAUDE.md records five rounds of v0.36.0 falsifying.
suggestion: Either widen §4's paragraph to two guards and name the second reversal precisely (the SKILL.md sentence becomes 'audit convergence counts every non-PASS row unless audit_converge_on is blocking', and docs_contract_test.go:96's constant moves with it), or drop the count and say 'the shipped guards this release reverses are:' followed by the list. Add the docs constant to §5 so an implementation that edits SKILL.md without moving the guard fails a test rather than the gate.

finding: §5's closing paragraph claims the untested surface is enumerated — 'What is not tested here, named so its absence is deliberate' — and names only role_streaks and spec_coverage_clean_rounds. The documentation surfaces are absent from both the tests and that list, while §2 makes them scope: 'review_converge_on as a shipped feature touches 16 production .go files, 11 test files, and both skills/tp/REFERENCE.md and skills/tp/SKILL.md ... Both are in this release's scope' (the sentence is about the two v0.31.1 surfaces, but the docs are named in the same breath and nothing else in the spec assigns them). REFERENCE.md's workflow-field table (:477 carries the audit_clean_rounds row) and SKILL.md's tp set --workflow row (:269 enumerates every settable field including review_converge_on) both need an entry, and the repository already has the guard shape for pinning them (docs_contract_test.go). As written, an implementation can pass all eleven tests with the field undocumented in both files — which is the failure mode §2 cites v0.31.1 as the price of.
suggestion: Add a test: 'REFERENCE.md's workflow-field table carries an audit_converge_on row with default all and the two legal values, and SKILL.md's tp set --workflow row names the field. Killing input: the shipped field with neither document updated.' Or, if the docs are deliberately out of scope, say so in the closing paragraph — it claims to be exhaustive.

finding: The spec cites ten unchanged sites to the line and never names the one line it changes. §2 pins engine/configresolve.go:261, engine/rolestreaks.go:128-142, internal/cli/unattended.go:56, set.go:414/:428, set_project.go:98/:108, escalate.go:41, review_record.go:231 and audit_signal_test.go:472 — every one of them a thing that stays as it is. The site that moves is internal/cli/audit_record.go:71, 'clean := findings == 0', where findings is countAuditFindings' total of non-PASS rows; that expression is the whole of today's audit cleanliness, and this release's deliverable is to break the identity it asserts. Two consequences follow from the same line and neither is stated: the value is passed to recordAuditRoundEntry (:85) and stamped into ReviewRound.Clean (:208), so under blocking the STORED flag changes meaning for every later reader of it — engine.ConsecutiveClean, engine.Converged, refuseIfBudgetExhausted (:52) and AuditNextAction via 'latestHasFindings := len(rounds) > 0 && !rounds[len(rounds)-1].Clean' (:390), which is what makes tp audit --status and tp resume recommend release instead of another round. That is presumably intended — it is the point of the field — but an implementer has to infer it, and the alternative reading (compute a severity-aware clean for the payload while stamping the old one) is equally consistent with §2 and produces a release that changes nothing.
suggestion: Name the site and the stamp: 'The change is at internal/cli/audit_record.go:71, where clean := findings == 0 becomes the audit_converge_on predicate over the same parsed rows. The value stamped into ReviewRound.Clean is the new one, so ConsecutiveClean, Converged, the round-budget refusal and AuditNextAction all read it — that propagation is the deliverable, not a side effect. findings keeps counting every non-PASS row.' (Distinct from round 5's derived-signals finding, which §2 answered for role_streaks and spec_coverage_clean_rounds; this is about the change site itself and the stored flag.)

finding: Third answer to the decomposability question, and this time it is YES for every section — the two blockers are gaps a repair closes, not decisions. Section by section: §1 yields no task (overview) and needs the stale-deliverable repair above; §2 yields six tasks; §2.1 yields the replay test; §2.2 yields no task of its own — its content is discharged by the fail-closed arm of the predicate task — and needs only its pointer fixed; §3 yields no task by construction, which is now correct and unambiguous; §4 yields one task (the guard reversal) and otherwise fences scope; §5 distributes its eleven tests across the tasks below with no test left unowned. Nothing here is a decision a review round cannot make: every acceptance sentence below is writable against the spec as it stands, except audit-converge-on-consuming-validation, which needs the §2 error-path repair first, and audit-converge-on-fence, whose acceptance I could only write by choosing the mechanism the spec leaves open (a policy predicate rather than fenceWorkflowWrite's cap path) and by leaving the =all case unstated. Both are gaps, both are one sentence each. The task list follows in the suggestion field.
suggestion:
Import list (id | title | depends_on | acceptance):

1. audit-converge-on-field | Add the audit_converge_on workflow field, its constants and its resolver | [] | audit_converge_on is a presence-tracked field on model.WorkflowOverride and a value on model.Workflow, resolving task override > project config > built-in `all` through engine.ResolveWorkflowLayers with no CLI and no environment layer. engine/auditconvergeon.go mirrors engine/reviewconvergeon.go: two constants, AuditConvergeOnHint = "must be one of: blocking, all", and ValidAuditConvergeOn shared by every caller. `tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=<bad>` and `tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=<bad>` each exit 2 with that hint and leave the file unmodified. Tests 1 and 2 pass; test 2's killing mutation (a resolver reading only the project layer) reddens it.

2. audit-clean-predicate | Make an audit round's clean flag severity-aware under blocking | ["audit-converge-on-field"] | Under `all` the stored and reported clean flag is unchanged (findings == 0). Under `blocking` a round is clean when no non-PASS row carries `error`; a non-PASS row whose severity is outside `error|warning|info`, null, or absent is counted as blocking. engine.SeverityRank is not consulted. The `findings` count, role_streaks[].open and spec_coverage_clean_rounds are byte-identical to today under both values. Tests 4, 5, 6 and 7 pass, test 7 over three fixtures (out-of-enum, null, absent).

NOTE: this task exists only if the spec adopts the §2 finding above — as written the spec specifies no consuming-command validation.

4. audit-converge-on-config-surfaces | Emit and validate the field in tp config --extract and tp validate --project | ["audit-converge-on-field"] | `tp config --extract` includes audit_converge_on in the common-policy computation and the emitted field list beside review_converge_on, and `tp config --resolved` reports its value and source; `tp validate --project` reports a task-file override that deviates from the project value and accepts an agreeing one. 5. audit-converge-on-fence | Fence both write paths under TP_UNATTENDED | ["audit-converge-on-field"] | `tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=blocking` and `tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=blocking` each exit 2 under TP_UNATTENDED=1 and 0 without it, with a hint naming the field a user-approved decision and pointing at tp escalate. The refusal is reached by a predicate of its own rather than by fenceWorkflowWrite's cap path, so engine.fencedCapFields and engine/unattended_test.go:69 are untouched. Test 9 passes and fails when either file's branch is left unfenced.

6. audit-converge-on-escalation-name | Add audit-converge-on to the --decision enum and map the field to it | ["audit-converge-on-fence"] | `audit-converge-on` is a member of the --decision enum in escalate.go and of engine.IsEscalationDecision, and the audit_converge_on refusal's hint names it rather than `other`; `tp escalate --decision audit-converge-on --evidence <text>` is accepted and records that decision name. Test 10 passes and reddens when the enum entry is removed.

7. audit-converge-on-replay-testdata | Pin §2.1's table as a replay over committed testdata | ["audit-clean-predicate"] | testdata/ carries the per-round (status, severity) rows of v0.35.0's nine and v0.36.0's thirteen recorded audit rounds with the source commit cited in the file. At audit_clean_rounds 2 the predicate reproduces §2.1: blocking converges at round 3 and all at round 9 for v0.35.0; blocking at 3 and all never for v0.36.0. The test reads nothing under spec/.tp-review/. Test 8 passes.

8. audit-converge-on-guard-reversal | Reverse exactly the two guard assertions the field invalidates | ["audit-converge-on-field"] | audit_signal_test.go:472-474 asserts that `tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=blocking` now exits 0 and persists the value, replacing the two unknown-field assertions. The other nine assert/require calls in TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate are unchanged and pass, including :498's assert.Len(t, e, 3), the wontfix-does-not-clear assertion and the --check-stays-shut assertion; signalRow still emits no severity key, so the round stays unclean under the fail-closed rule. Test 11 passes.

9. audit-converge-on-docs | Document the field in REFERENCE.md and SKILL.md and move the pinned sentence | ["audit-clean-predicate","audit-converge-on-fence"] | REFERENCE.md's workflow-field table carries an audit_converge_on row (string, default all, values blocking|all, settable) and its fence section names the field; SKILL.md's `tp set --workflow` row names it. The SKILL.md sentence pinned by docs_contract_test.go:96 is restated so it is true under both values, and the test's constant moves with it. The full quality gate passes.
